name: GSV-Cities
summary: Official training and evaluation code for the GSV-Cities visual place recognition dataset (about 530k street-level images of 62k+ places across many cities), including the Conv-AP aggregator and evaluation notebooks for standard VPR benchmarks.
why_it_matters: The standard large training set for modern VPR descriptors; training without offline triplet mining makes fine-tuning on your own imagery fast.
hackathon_notes: Dataset is on Kaggle under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (research only); the code repo has no licence file. Use it to pretrain or fine-tune a descriptor, then adapt to aerial tiles. Last push 2024.

name: OpenVPRLab
summary: Modular PyTorch framework for training VPR models as data -> backbone -> aggregation -> loss, with one-command download of GSV-Cities / GSV-Cities-light, metric-learning losses, TensorBoard logging and retrieval visualizations.
why_it_matters: Fastest route to training or fine-tuning your own place-recognition model with swappable aggregators.
hackathon_notes: Conda environment install; GSV-Cities-light is the quick start. MIT licence on code, but the GSV-Cities data is CC BY-NC-ND. No commits since mid-2024.

name: aero-vloc
summary: Benchmark tool accompanying the aerial VPR survey by Moskalenko et al.: downloads satellite map tiles, localizes UAV imagery against them with AnyLoc, CosPlace, EigenPlaces, MixVPR, NetVLAD, SALAD or SelaVPR, and optionally re-ranks with LightGlue, SuperGlue or SelaVPR.
why_it_matters: Ready-made drone-to-satellite VPR pipeline with many descriptors behind one interface, plus evidence on how tile zoom and overlap affect recall.
hackathon_notes: Start from example.ipynb (download map, localize a sequence, compute recall). Some weights come from a Google Drive link, others via TorchHub. Tested on Python 3.10. Apache-2.0.

name: Deep Visual Geo-localization Benchmark
summary: Official code for the CVPR 2022 benchmark: a configurable training and evaluation framework for visual geo-localization where backbone, aggregation, negative mining and pre/post-processing can be swapped and measured.
why_it_matters: Lets a team compare VPR design choices on equal footing, including runtime and memory, before committing to an onboard model.
hackathon_notes: Datasets must be arranged in its directory layout; the VPR-datasets-downloader repo helps. MIT licence.

name: Matlab-LagrangianPMF
summary: MATLAB implementation of Lagrangian grid-based (point-mass) filters for terrain-aided navigation, compared against other filters on real-world-based TAN models, with code for several related papers including the tensor-decomposition variant.
why_it_matters: State-of-the-art grid filters for terrain-aided navigation that run in real time; a strong alternative to particle filters for radar-altimeter TRN.
hackathon_notes: Needs MATLAB; a mex file speeds the FFT time update and can be switched off. AGPL-3.0 licence matters if you ship derived code.

name: efficient-PMF
summary: MATLAB code for the efficient point-mass filter (FUSION 2023) for systems with linear state dynamics, illustrated on terrain-aided navigation.
why_it_matters: Small, readable reference implementation of a fast grid-based TAN filter.
hackathon_notes: Needs MATLAB; no licence file. The pesslovany/Matlab-LagrangianPMF repo is the maintained successor.

name: UWB drone dataset (TIERS)
summary: Dataset, ROS nodes and DWM1001 firmware from the IROS 2020 paper on UWB localization for autonomous UAV flight: several anchor configurations, flights inside and outside the anchor hull, and an anchor auto-positioning method.
why_it_matters: Cheap Decawave hardware recipe plus real flight data for UWB-aided GNSS-denied flight.
hackathon_notes: Use the data to tune a UWB EKF before buying hardware. No licence file. Not updated since 2022.

name: RCV UWB relative-pose dataset
summary: Drone UWB dataset: six flight sequences with two-way ranging to four anchors, stereo VIO, motion-capture ground truth for drone and anchors, CSV exports and an analysis tool; rosbags on Google Drive.
why_it_matters: Shows how anchor and tag orientation bias UWB ranges, which is what breaks naive UWB models in practice.
hackathon_notes: CSV files are usable without ROS. No licence file, so reuse terms are unstated.
